name: com.kibootia.backend.AdminApiTest
comment:
The base of the integration tests that drive the identity, access and audit APIs through the real stack: filter chain, request gate, method security, decision point, MySQL, with a fake in place of Keycloak. Every subclass has the same configuration, so they share one Spring context and one MySQL container.

The base knows no feature module beyond the core ones: it imports {@link WidgetFixtures} for permissions to work with and a protected URL, and never names the notes module. A test that creates notes cleans the note table itself.

{@link #ADMIN} is the bootstrap administrator: the first request they make with a verified email address grants the administrator role, exactly as in production ({@code kibootia.identity.bootstrap-admin-email}). Everyone else starts with the built-in user role only.

methods.name: ensureAdmin
methods.comment: Makes the bootstrap administrator exist by letting them make their first request.

methods.name: signIn
methods.comment: Lets the user make their first request, so their profile exists, and returns their ID.

methods.name: builtInRoleId
methods.comment: The ID of a built-in role: {@code ADMIN} or {@code USER}.

methods.name: createRole
methods.comment: Creates a role as the administrator and returns its ID.

methods.name: setRoles
methods.comment: Sets the roles of a user as the administrator.

methods.name: makeAdministrator
methods.comment: Makes the user an administrator without going through the API, so a test can set a situation up. The user must have made a first request, so the built-in roles exist.

name: com.kibootia.backend.ArchitectureRulesFireTest
comment: The architecture rules are only worth having if they can fail. Most rules say "no class may...", which a typo in a package name, or a module that does not exist, makes true of nothing; so each rule here is also pointed at a class made to break it, and at one made to satisfy it. The classes are under {@code platform.archfixtures} in the test sources: they are not beans, and neither {@code ArchitectureTest} nor Spring Modulith looks at test classes.

name: com.kibootia.backend.ArchitectureTest
comment: ArchUnit rules from kibootia-docs/architecture/architecture-enforcement.md. Rule 5 covers every removable module in {@link #REMOVABLE_MODULES}; rules 2 and 3 are covered by Spring Modulith ({@code ModularityTest}). Because the notes module can be removed, a rule must not need any particular feature module to exist: a rule about a module that is absent simply has nothing to check.

methods.name: rule5_nothingOutsideARemovableModuleDependsOnIt
methods.comment: Rule 5 for every removable default-on module (ADR 0024): nothing outside it depends on it, so removing it, or switching it off, cannot break another module. Others reach {@code files} through the {@code platform.files} port; nothing reaches {@code notes}, which is only a consumer.

name: com.kibootia.backend.AuthorizationRules
comment: Architecture rule 7 (ADR 0044): every public use-case method carries an authorization check or an explicit {@code @NoAuthorization("reason")}. A use case is a Spring component in an {@code application} package. A method counts as checked when it is annotated {@code @RequiresPermission}, or calls {@code Authorization} directly. A check made inside a lambda or a helper class is not seen; put the call in the method itself, or mark it {@code @NoAuthorization} with the reason.

name: com.kibootia.backend.AuthorizationRulesTest
comment: Proves rule 7 fails for an unprotected use case and passes for protected ones. The fixtures are nested classes of this test, which Spring never scans; they live in this test's package, which is the package the rule is pointed at.

name: com.kibootia.backend.Await
comment: Waits for something that happens on another thread, such as an asynchronous event delivery.

methods.name: until
methods.comment: Returns when the condition holds; fails the test if it does not within the timeout.

name: com.kibootia.backend.BackendApplicationIT
comment: Starts the whole application against MySQL: Flyway migrates from an empty database and Hibernate validates the mapped tables (including the event publication registry) against the migrated schema.

name: com.kibootia.backend.EventAndJobRules
comment: Architecture rules 9 to 11 for scheduled jobs and durable events (ADR 0031, ADR 0039).

methods.name: scheduledMethodsTakeALock
methods.comment: Rule 9: with several instances, an unlocked job runs on all of them at once.

methods.name: durableListenersReplaceApplicationModuleListener
methods.comment: Rule 10: {@code @ApplicationModuleListener} opens its transaction before the tenant is known, so Hibernate would bind the session to no tenant. {@code @DurableEventListener} binds the tenant first.

methods.name: durableListenersTakeADomainEvent
methods.comment: Rule 11: the wrapper needs the event's context to restore the tenant and trace.

name: com.kibootia.backend.EventAndJobRulesTest
comment: Proves rules 9 to 11 fail for the mistakes they exist for and pass for correct code.

name: com.kibootia.backend.FakeIdentityProvider
comment:
Stands in for Keycloak in every integration test except {@code KeycloakAdminAdapterIT}. It keeps accounts in memory, records what it was asked to do, and can be told to fail, so the tests can show that a Keycloak outage delays a change without losing it.

A user it was never told about counts as an enabled account with a verified address: tests sign in as arbitrary IDs, and Keycloak knowing them is the normal case. {@link #goneFromKeycloak} makes one unknown, as after an erasure.

methods.name: reset
methods.comment: Forgets everything: accounts, calls and failures.

methods.name: register
methods.comment: Registers an account with these properties.

methods.name: knowsEmail
methods.comment: Keycloak already has an account for this address (lower case), so creating one answers "email in use".

methods.name: goneFromKeycloak
methods.comment: Keycloak no longer knows this user, as after an erasure.

methods.name: failNext
methods.comment: The next {@code times} calls of this kind fail as if Keycloak were down. Kinds are the method names.

methods.name: failEverything
methods.comment: Every call fails until {@link #reset}.

methods.name: calls
methods.comment: What was asked, in order, such as {@code sendInvitation:<id>}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.FakeObjectStorage
comment: An in-memory object store for tests that are about the module and not about S3, which {@code S3ObjectStorageContractIT} covers against a real server. It can be made to fail, to stand for a storage outage, and its objects can be made to look old, so the reconciliation grace period can be tested without waiting.

methods.name: setUnavailable
methods.comment: Makes every call fail with {@link ObjectStorage.Unavailable} until switched back.

methods.name: putAt
methods.comment: Stores bytes under a key as if they had been written at the given time.

methods.name: backdate
methods.comment: Makes an existing object look as if it had been written at the given time.

name: com.kibootia.backend.GrantedPermissions
comment: Lets a test act as an administrator before roles exist (milestone 3). On top of the built-in {@code user} role, a caller holds whatever the test has {@link #grant granted}. Import it into a test; call {@link #reset} after each test.

name: com.kibootia.backend.ModularityTest
comment: Spring Modulith verification: no cycles between modules, no access to the internals of another module.

methods.name: coreModulesExist
methods.comment: The core modules are always there. The default-on modules ({@code files}, {@code notes}) are not required, because a fork may remove them (ADR 0024); what they may and may not depend on is checked by rule 5 in {@code ArchitectureTest}, and the verification below covers whatever modules exist.

methods.name: everyModuleIsKnown
methods.comment: Every module is one of the known ones, so a stray package cannot become a module unnoticed.

methods.name: coreModulesDependOnEachOtherSoVerificationHasSomethingToCheck
methods.comment: Verification only means something if the modules depend on each other: with no edges there is no cycle to find and no internal access to refuse. Spring Modulith ignores test classes, so a broken module cannot be fed to it from the test sources; this shows instead that the real graph has edges, among the core modules that are always present.

name: com.kibootia.backend.ModuleRules
comment: Architecture rule 5 (ADR 0024) as a rule that can be pointed at any module, real or a test fixture.

methods.name: nothingOutsideDependsOn
methods.comment: Nothing outside the module may depend on it, so removing it, or switching it off, cannot break another module.

name: com.kibootia.backend.ModuleStartupIT
comment: What must be true of the application whichever default-on modules a fork removed or switched off (ADR 0024). It is the test group the module-removal CI job runs for every row of its matrix (together with the migrate-from-empty test): the application starts against MySQL, the core API answers, and a module that is off or gone says so instead of failing. It names no removable module by class, so it compiles with any of them deleted, and it reads the switches from the environment the job set.

name: com.kibootia.backend.TestcontainersConfiguration
comment: Real MySQL for integration tests, the same major version as {@code compose.yaml}, and a fake in place of Keycloak. The connection replaces the datasource settings, so no local password is needed; the fake means no test needs a Keycloak unless it is about the Keycloak adapter itself.

methods.name: fakeIdentityProvider
methods.comment: Takes the place of the Keycloak adapter wherever an {@code IdentityProviderAdmin} is injected.

methods.name: fakeObjectStorage
methods.comment: Takes the place of the S3 adapter wherever an {@code ObjectStorage} is injected, so no test needs a storage server unless it is about the adapter itself ({@code S3ObjectStorageContractIT}).

name: com.kibootia.backend.academic.AcademicApiTest
comment:
For a module's test that needs people who hold Timetia roles in places (W4.2): a base class that seeds the six roles and a small campus, signs people in and gives them roles through the real API, and asks the real decision point what they may do. A test reads as the story it tells: 
{@code UUID hod = hodOf(DEPARTMENT_A); UUID cr = crOf(DIVISION_1); assertThat(can(hod, AcademicPermissions.TICKETS_REVERT, ticketInDepartmentA)).isTrue(); assertThat(can(hod, AcademicPermissions.TICKETS_REVERT, ticketInDepartmentB)).isFalse(); }

The campus is fixed (see {@link Facts}): department A ({@code CSE}) holds division 1 ({@code CSE-A}) and its batch 1 ({@code CSE-A1}); department B ({@code ME}) holds division 2 ({@code ME-A}) and its batch 2 ({@code ME-A1}). Places are known to a stand-in scope directory, because the application has no provider of its own yet. The people are given roles exactly as the screen does, so everything the application enforces when it gives a role is enforced here too.

Everything is read from the database on every call, like a request, so a role removed with {@link #unassign} stops working at once.

methods.name: seedCampus
methods.comment: Runs after the base class has emptied the database: the campus, the six roles and the administrator.

methods.name: somebody
methods.comment: A signed-in person with no role beyond the default one.

methods.name: personWith
methods.comment: A person who holds the role in the department, division or batch, given by the administrator as the screen does.

methods.name: assign
methods.comment: Gives an existing person one more role (a place for a scoped role; null for a role that applies everywhere).

methods.name: unassign
methods.comment: Takes one role away; it stops working on the person's next request.

methods.name: asCaller
methods.comment: Runs the work as the person, in the default tenant, as a request with their verified token would.

methods.name: runAs
methods.comment: The same for work that returns nothing. A separate name, so a lambda is never ambiguous between the two.

methods.name: can
methods.comment: Whether the person may do the action to the record described by the facts.

methods.name: reachOf
methods.comment: How far the person's permission reaches, for a list.

name: com.kibootia.backend.academic.AcademicAuthorizationIT
comment: Timetia's authorization through the real stack: roles seeded in MySQL, scoped assignments through the API, the decision point, the grants read from the database on every call and the academic policy. The unit test of the policy proves each rule; this proves that the pieces are wired so that a person gets what their assignments give them, in the place they hold it, and nothing more, from the next request on.

methods.name: as
methods.comment: Runs the work as the signed-in user, in the default tenant, as a request would.

name: com.kibootia.backend.academic.AuthorizationWorkedExampleIT
comment:
The worked example (W4.1): how a module that owns tickets uses authorization, written as it would be in that module and run against the real decision point, the real roles and a real database. {@link ExampleTickets} is the model.

The module's own parts are the table, the facts it builds from a row, and the state rules. Security's parts are the two calls: {@code authorization.can}/{@code require} for one record, and {@code authorization.reach} for a list. The list is the only place a module can get this wrong silently, so the test proves it agrees with the single-record decision for every person and every ticket.

methods.name: facts
methods.comment: The facts the policy needs, built from the module's own record. In a real module the entity or a small adapter implements {@link TicketAccessFacts}; the module, not security, knows its people and its places.

name: com.kibootia.backend.academic.AuthorizationWorkedExampleIT$ExampleTickets
comment: What a module writes. Everything about authorization is in {@link #mayView}, {@link #list} and {@link #revert}.

methods.name: get
methods.comment: One record the caller may see, or 404. Check visibility first so a forbidden record is not revealed.

methods.name: mayView
methods.comment: The caller may see it through their place (HOD, CR, BR, Super HOD) or because they are on it (faculty).

methods.name: revert
methods.comment: 404 if not visible, 403 if visible and not allowed, then the module's own state rule.

methods.name: list
methods.comment: A list is filtered in the query, on the module's own columns, from the caller's reach. Never load everything and filter in memory, and never page before filtering.

name: com.kibootia.backend.academic.Facts
comment: Facts for the tests: one record that is a lecture, a ticket and an issue at once, so a test can build the situation it needs with {@link #lecture} and the {@code with...} methods and ask about it. Ids are fixed so that tests read as stories: department A holds division 1 with batch 1, department B holds division 2 with batch 2.

methods.name: lecture
methods.comment: A lecture of division 1 in department A, for batch 1, that nobody teaches yet and no ticket concerns.

methods.name: inDepartmentB
methods.comment: The same lecture in department B, division 2, batch 2.

methods.name: withoutPlace
methods.comment: A lecture that says nothing about where it is, to prove that missing facts never match a grant.

name: com.kibootia.backend.academic.domain.AcademicAccessPolicyTest
comment: Every rule of the role and scope model, allowed and denied, with the cross-department, cross-division and cross-batch cases that the model exists to prevent. The tests state the documented rule, not the code's branches.

name: com.kibootia.backend.academic.domain.AcademicAccessPolicyTest$LectureOnly
comment: A lecture and nothing else: it has no author, no reviewers and no opener.

name: com.kibootia.backend.academic.domain.AcademicRolesTest
comment: The seeded roles against the role by permission table in the role and scope model document. The expected values are written out here by name, not taken from the constants, so a change to a template or a permission name has to be made on purpose in two places.

name: com.kibootia.backend.access.AccessApiIT
comment: Roles, permissions and assignments through the real stack (ADR 0025, ADR 0044): every operation has an allowed and a denied case, role editing cannot be used to escalate, the administrator safeguards hold, and a change applies on the next request.

name: com.kibootia.backend.access.AccessConfigurationTest$FlatCheckOfPolicyDecided
comment: A permission only a record check can satisfy, protected by the permission-only annotation: a mistake.

name: com.kibootia.backend.access.ScopedAssignmentsApiIT
comment: Giving roles within a scope, and the rules that keep scoped roles apart from platform roles (Timetia ADR 0004): who may give them, what a request must say, what is refused and what is audited.

name: com.kibootia.backend.access.ScopedAssignmentsWithoutDirectoryIT
comment: When nothing can tell whether a place exists (the reference module is absent or its provider is not there), a role that needs a place is refused, so nothing is silently unvalidated; a role that applies everywhere needs no place and still works (Timetia ADR 0004). This context has no scope directory, unlike the application, which now has one.

name: com.kibootia.backend.access.TwoInstancesIT
comment: Role changes apply on the next request on every instance (ADR 0044, milestone 3). There is no permission cache to invalidate: each decision reads the roles from MySQL. This starts a second, separate application context on the same database, as a second instance would be, and shows that it sees a change the first one just made, in both directions.

name: com.kibootia.backend.access.application.BuiltInRolesIT
comment: What starting the application does to the built-in roles (ADR 0041): it offers the user role each permission a module flags for it, once, so an administrator's removals are still there after the next start.

name: com.kibootia.backend.access.domain.PolicyDecidedPermissionsTest
comment: Policy-decided permissions (Timetia ADR 0004): the flat checks never satisfy them, a record check needs the permission through some assignment and a policy that supports the record, and a policy can narrow but never grant.

name: com.kibootia.backend.access.domain.PolicyDecidedPermissionsTest$RecordingPolicy
comment: A policy that supports tickets, records what it was asked, and answers as told.

name: com.kibootia.backend.audit.application.AuditLogIT
comment: The audit log on a real MySQL (ADR 0046): one entry per change in the same transaction, none for a rolled-back change, the actor and tenant taken from the caller, no personal data, and the retention purge.

name: com.kibootia.backend.audit.application.AuditViewerIT
comment: The audit log viewer (ADR 0046): only for those who may view it, newest first, filterable, with names looked up when an entry is shown and a user who was erased shown as erased.

name: com.kibootia.backend.audit.application.SecurityEventsIT
comment: Refusals of signed-in users are recorded as security events (Timetia ADR 0005): who, which permission or code, and nothing personal. An unauthenticated request is not recorded, because anyone could cause unlimited writes.

name: com.kibootia.backend.audit.application.SecurityEventsThrottleIT
comment: A flood of refused requests from one user cannot fill the audit log: only the first few in a minute are recorded (Timetia ADR 0005). The answer to the caller is the same whether the event was recorded or dropped.

name: com.kibootia.backend.audit.web.FailedEventsApiIT
comment: The failed-event API (ADR 0031): administrators see events that keep failing and retry them, every retry is audited, and everyone else is refused. Each operation has an allowed and a denied case.

name: com.kibootia.backend.files.FileJobsIT
comment: The jobs and the event of the files module (ADR 0029, ADR 0034): the retention purge removes deleted files and their objects once the period has passed, reconciliation removes objects nothing refers to once they are old enough to be sure no upload is still being written, and erasing a user removes everything they stored at once.

methods.name: file
methods.comment: A file row with both objects present. {@code createdDaysAgo} ages the row; {@code deletedDaysAgo} null keeps it live.

name: com.kibootia.backend.files.FilesDisabledIT
comment: The files module can be switched off with {@code kibootia.files.enabled=false} (ADR 0024): the application starts with no storage setting and none of the module's beans, everything else works, and the avatar endpoints say why they do not. This is the detailed module-removal check for {@code files}; the CI job {@code module-removal} also starts the whole application with the module off and runs the {@code startup} test group (see {@code ModuleStartupIT}).

name: com.kibootia.backend.files.application.ImageProcessorTest
comment: What happens to an uploaded image (ADR 0029): every rendition is a new PNG made from the pixels, either the centred square or the whole image with its proportions, turned upright by the EXIF orientation, with nothing of the original left in it, and an image too large to decode safely is refused before it is decoded.

methods.name: redBlue
methods.comment: Left half red, right half blue.

methods.name: segment
methods.comment: A segment of a JPEG: the marker, the length (which counts its own two bytes) and the data.

methods.name: exifWithOrientation
methods.comment: An EXIF block with one entry, the orientation, and a text that must not survive.

methods.name: withSegments
methods.comment: The JPEG with extra segments right after its start marker, where a camera puts its EXIF and comment.

name: com.kibootia.backend.files.s3.S3ObjectStorageContractIT
comment:
The storage contract against the S3 API of the pinned RustFS (ADR 0029). This is the verification gate of OQ-40: the operations the module needs, including presigned PUT and GET, must work on the local default server, or SeaweedFS becomes the default. Because the module talks to the S3 API only, running these same tests against another server is a change of the container below.

The credentials are generated for each run in the shape {@code pnpm bootstrap} uses (43 URL-safe characters, which can contain {@code -} and {@code _}), so a value that a server mishandles shows up here and not on a developer's machine, and no secret-looking literal is committed.

methods.name: generatedKey
methods.comment: Made the way {@code pnpm bootstrap} makes a secret: 32 random bytes as 43 URL-safe characters.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.AvatarApiIT
comment: The avatar flow through the real stack (ADR 0029, ADR 0041): upload, replace, view and delete, who may see whose avatar, tenant isolation, what an upload may be, and what happens when the storage server is down. The storage server is the in-memory fake; {@code S3ObjectStorageContractIT} covers the real one.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.AvatarRateLimitIT
comment: Uploads use the {@code uploads} category of the rate limiter built in milestone 3: past a user's allowance an upload is 429 with {@code Retry-After}, nothing is stored for it, and another user is not affected. Viewing is not limited.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.IdentityGateIT
comment: The request gate and the signed-in user's own account (ADR 0041): a profile created on first use, the built-in role, name and email refreshed from the token, a disabled or deleted user refused from the next request, and what an unverified user may and may not do.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.UserAdministrationIT
comment: What an administrator does with other people's accounts (ADR 0041): inviting, disabling, deleting, restoring and erasing, each with an allowed and a denied case, audited once, with Keycloak brought in line by durable events that survive an outage and repeat harmlessly.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.UserImportIT
comment: The provisioning import (Timetia ADR 0006, W3.1): what it creates, that a repeat changes nothing, that it never goes beyond what the screen would allow, and what it leaves alone. The tests that need no places are in {@link UserImportWithoutDirectoryIT}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.UserImportLimitsIT
comment: The limits that keep an import bounded (Timetia ADR 0006): how often real imports may run, and how long one may take. The base class's own limits are lifted for every other test, so these run in a context of their own.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.UserImportWithoutDirectoryIT
comment: When nothing provides departments, divisions and batches, the import cannot check a place and must not guess. Rows for roles that apply everywhere work; every row that names a place is refused, and a person with such a row is left out entirely (Timetia ADR 0004 and 0006). This context has no scope directory, unlike the application, which now has one.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.application.BootstrapAdministratorIT
comment: How a fresh environment gets its first Super Admin without anyone touching the database (Timetia ADR 0006, W3.3): the application invites the configured address at startup when nobody is an administrator, and the person becomes administrator when they first sign in, once. The runner has already run once when this context started, against an empty database; each test cleans up and runs it again, as a restart would.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.application.BootstrapAdministratorInvitationTest
comment: The cases where the setting says nothing usable: the runner must neither fail nor touch anything.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.application.ImportCsvTest
comment: What the import file may look like, and what is refused before any person is looked at.

name: com.kibootia.backend.identity.keycloak.KeycloakAdminAdapterIT
comment: The Keycloak adapter against a real Keycloak and a real mail catcher (ADR 0025, ADR 0041, ADR 0045), with the least-privilege service account the design calls for: the realm-management roles to view, query and manage users, and nothing else. It shows that the account can create, find, disable, enable and delete users and have Keycloak send both emails, that a client holding fewer roles is refused, and that a wrong secret or an unreachable server is reported without leaking anything.

methods.name: mailTo
methods.comment: The mail the catcher holds for an address, as its raw JSON.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.NoteAttachmentApiIT
comment: The picture of a note through the real stack (ADR 0029, ADR 0051): attach, replace, view and remove, who may see and change it, tenant isolation, what happens to it when the note is deleted, restored, purged or its owner is erased, and what an upload may be. The storage server is the in-memory fake; {@code S3ObjectStorageContractIT} covers the real one.

methods.name: noteOf
methods.comment: A note of the user, made through the API.

methods.name: attachedNoteOf
methods.comment: A note of the user with a picture, and the ID of the stored file.

methods.name: grant
methods.comment: Gives the user a role holding the permissions, on top of the built-in user role.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.NoteAttachmentFilesDisabledIT
comment: With the files module switched off (ADR 0024) the notes work as before and only the picture says why it cannot: the attachment endpoints answer 404 {@code files.disabled}, the profile says files are off, and purging a note that still has a file from the time files were on does not fail.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.NoteAttachmentRateLimitIT
comment: A note's picture uses the {@code uploads} category of the rate limiter, like an avatar: past a user's allowance an upload is 429 with {@code Retry-After}, nothing is stored for it, and another user is not affected. A caller who is refused for who they are spends none of their allowance, because the limit is applied after the permission check.

methods.name: deniedUploadsAreNotCounted
methods.comment: The limiter keeps its state for the whole run, per user, so each test uses users of its own. This one uses Carol, who may see anyone's notes but change none, and Dave's note as the one she tries.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.NoteErasureIT
comment: Erasing a user removes the notes they own and no one else's (ADR 0034, ADR 0041). This is the notes module's part of the {@code UserErased} event, so it lives with the module; the user administration tests do not know about notes.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.NotesApiIT
comment: The reference feature through the real stack: filter chain, tenant, method security, decision point, MySQL (ADR 0043, ADR 0044, ADR 0034). Every operation has an allowed and a denied case, lists test their scope, and the soft-delete, tenant-isolation, locking and purge conventions are shown on a real resource.

methods.name: noteOfAnotherTenant
methods.comment: A live note of another tenant, written straight into the table.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.NotesOpenApiIT
comment: What the notes module adds to the API description. The core test ({@code OpenApiContractIT}) leaves these paths and types out so that it stays right when the module is removed; this one goes with the module.

name: com.kibootia.backend.notes.application.NoteAttachmentServiceTest
comment: The parts of the attachment rules that are plain logic. The order of the checks (note visible, then allowed, then the upload allowance is spent, then the file is stored) needs the real decision point and is covered through the API in {@code NoteAttachmentApiIT} and {@code NoteAttachmentRateLimitIT}.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.EventPublicationRegistryIT
comment: Proves the Spring Modulith event publication registry works on MySQL with the Flyway-created table: an event published in a transaction is stored, delivered to its listener and marked completed.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.bad.application.UncheckedUseCase
comment: A use case with a public method and no authorization check. Rule 7 must name it. Not a bean (see ArchitectureRulesFireTest).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.bad.events.LegacyListener
comment: A listener that opens its transaction before the tenant is bound. Rule 10 must name it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.bad.events.WrongParameterListener
comment: A durable listener that does not take a domain event, so the tenant cannot be restored. Rule 11 must name it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.bad.jobs.UnlockedJob
comment: A scheduled method with no lock: on several instances it would run on all of them at once. Rule 9 must name it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.good.application.CheckedUseCase
comment: A use case where every public method is checked or explicitly marked. Rule 7 must accept it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.good.events.CorrectListener
comment: A durable listener that takes a domain event. Rule 11 must accept it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.good.jobs.LockedJob
comment: A scheduled method under a lock. Rule 9 must accept it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.rule5.core.DependsOnRemovable
comment: Core code that needs a removable module, so the module could not be removed. Rule 5 must name it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.rule5.lonely.Lonely
comment: A removable module nobody depends on. Rule 5 must accept it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.archfixtures.rule5.removable.Widget
comment: The class of a removable module that something outside it wrongly depends on.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.authorization.AuthorizationIT
comment: Authorization through the real context: {@code @RequiresPermission} enforced by method security, the decision point from the {@code access} module, record checks, scopes, the system caller and the 403 the API returns. Each protected operation has an allowed and a denied case (verification standard).

methods.name: complete
methods.comment: An environment that has every required setting except the ones a test then leaves out or changes.

methods.name: production
methods.comment: Every address a real deployment must set, and a management port apart from the API port.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.DurableEventsIT
comment: Durable events on a real MySQL (ADR 0031, ADR 0039): tenant and trace restored in the handler, a repeated delivery skipped, retry with backoff and a cap, the failed-event view, and a manual retry. Backoff is zero here so the retry job can be driven by hand; {@link RetryPolicyTest} covers the waits.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.FlakyListener
comment: A test listener that fails a chosen number of times and records what the wrapper gave it. Import it into a test; it is a {@code @TestComponent}, so no other test sees it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.FlakyListener$Seen
comment: What the handler saw when it ran.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.events.FlakyListener$TestEvent
comment: An event raised by a test.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.fixtures.ScopeDirectoryContract
comment:
What every {@link ScopeDirectory} must do, as a test the owner of department, division and batch data extends (Timetia ADR 0004 and 0006, integration contract). The security code relies on exactly these answers to decide whether a role may be given in a place, and it never checks them again, so a provider that breaks one of them lets a role be given in a place that does not exist, or in the wrong one.

To use it, extend this class in the provider's own test, build the provider against a test database, and implement the three hooks to create and delete places the way the module itself would. The hooks act on the current tenant unless they say otherwise. Nothing here assumes how codes are compared (case, spaces): that is the provider's rule. It only requires that the rule is applied the same way every time and that a code never names two places.

{@code ScopeDirectoryContractTest} runs it against the test double, so the double is held to the same rules.

methods.name: newDirectory
methods.comment: A fresh provider with no places, for the current tenant. Called before every test.

methods.name: addPlace
methods.comment: Adds a live place of this kind with this code to the current tenant.

methods.name: deletePlace
methods.comment: Deletes the place the way the owning module does: it is no longer live.

methods.name: addPlaceInAnotherTenant
methods.comment: Adds a live place to another tenant. A provider has to prove that tenants are separate; a test double with no notion of a tenant records the place somewhere it is never read.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.fixtures.ScopeDirectoryContractTest
comment: Holds the test double to the same rules as a real provider ({@link ScopeDirectoryContract}), so the tests that use it do not pass on behaviour the real one is not allowed to have. The provider's own test extends the contract the same way.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.fixtures.ScopeFixtures
comment: A light stand-in for the places the reference module owns: it knows only the places a test adds, so an authorization test need not create real departments in the database. The reference module now provides a real {@code ScopeDirectory} that is always a bean, so this fake is marked {@link Primary}: a test that imports these fixtures gets the fake, while a test that does not (and production) uses the real provider. Imported by the tests that assign scoped roles.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.fixtures.ScopeFixtures$FakeScopeDirectory
comment: The places that exist, by kind and id, and the codes of those that have one. Codes compare exactly.

methods.name: add
methods.comment: A place that can be named by its code.

methods.name: setUnavailable
methods.comment: Makes every question throw, as a provider whose database or service is down would. {@link #clear()} resets it.

methods.name: remove
methods.comment: A place that was deleted: it is no longer found by id or by code, as the contract requires.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.fixtures.WidgetFixtures
comment:
A stand-in feature for the tests of the platform, access and identity modules: permissions with the same shape as a real feature's (some every user holds, some that must be granted, {@code -any} variants that widen "mine" to "everyone's") and one protected endpoint pair. Those tests need some declared permissions and some protected URL to work against; naming a real feature there would stop the application's tests from passing once that feature is removed. Imported by {@code AdminApiTest}, so every integration test built on it has it.

The widgets do not exist as data: the endpoints only check the permission and answer. They are not part of the application and never appear in {@code openapi.json}, which is generated from a context that does not import this.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.fixtures.WidgetFixtures$WidgetsApi
comment: Two endpoints that need a permission and nothing else, for tests that need a protected URL.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.fixtures.WithoutScopeDirectory
comment: A context in which nothing can say whether a department, division or batch exists. The application always has such a provider now (the reference module), but the code that asks must still fail closed when there is none, so that nothing is ever silently unvalidated: a role that needs a place is refused and a role that applies everywhere still works. A test of that path imports this to take every {@link ScopeDirectory} out of the context.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.jobs.JobLockIT
comment: Lock-protected jobs on a real MySQL (ADR 0031). Two callers stand in for two application instances: they share only the database.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.jobs.JobsEnabledIT
comment: With jobs switched on, the scheduled jobs really take their lock in the database.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.jobs.RetentionPurgeJobIT
comment: The retention purge (ADR 0034, ADR 0046): one job removes expired audit entries, delivered events and processed marks as the system, in the default tenant, and a purge that fails does not stop the others.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.observability.TraceLoggingIT
comment: The console log is structured JSON and carries the ID of the active trace (observability baseline, ADR 0030).

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence.PersistenceConventionsIT
comment: The persistence conventions on a real MySQL (ADR 0028, 0033, 0034; OQ-41): UUIDv7 keys in BINARY(16), audit columns, optimistic locking, tenant isolation and soft delete, using a test-only table.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.persistence.TestWidget
comment: A test-only entity that exercises the persistence base types.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.ratelimit.RateLimitIT
comment: The in-app rate limiter on the sensitive endpoints (API conventions, threat model): invitations, verification mail and administrative actions answer 429 with {@code Retry-After} once a user's allowance is used up, and one user's allowance does not affect another's.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.ResourceServerIT
comment: The resource server against a real decoder and a local key endpoint (token-validation.md, ADR 0008). Each rejection case of milestone 1 has its own test.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.security.TestKeys
comment: Signing keys and a local JWKS endpoint for the resource-server tests. The endpoint runs on a random local port while tokens carry the public Keycloak issuer, which is how the real deployment splits the two (ADR 0040).

methods.name: validToken
methods.comment: A token for a signed-in user that passes every check.

methods.name: unsignedToken
methods.comment: A token with the right claims and no signature at all ({@code alg: none}).

methods.name: tokenSignedWithSharedSecret
methods.comment: A token with the right claims signed with a shared secret instead of Keycloak's RSA key.

methods.name: baseClaims
methods.comment: The claims of an access token Keycloak would issue to a signed-in user.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web.ApiConventionsIT
comment: The HTTP conventions of ADR 0043 through the real filter chain and controller advice: one error shape for every failure, the status table, and paging. A test-only controller (nested, so no other test sees it) raises each failure.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web.ApiDocsExposureIT
comment: The API documentation is reachable only when asked for (ADR 0043): by default neither the description nor Swagger UI is served anywhere, and when exposed they live on the internal management port, never on the API port.

name: com.kibootia.backend.platform.web.OpenApiContractIT
comment: Writes the OpenAPI description to the committed {@code backend/openapi.json} (ADR 0043). The frontend client is generated from that file, and CI fails when running the build changes it: an API change is therefore always visible as a diff in the pull request. Run {@code ./mvnw verify} and commit the result after changing an endpoint.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.CampusAdminApiIT
comment: Drives the campus admin APIs through the real stack (ADR 0043 conventions, CONFIG_MANAGE). Unlike {@code AcademicApiTest}, this test does not import the fake scope directory, so the real {@code JpaScopeDirectory} is what answers: the end-to-end test proves a scoped role can finally be assigned in a department created over HTTP, which was the one thing blocking Timetia's scoped roles.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.CatalogAdminApiIT
comment: Drives the reference catalog APIs (subjects, rooms, faculty, terms) through the real stack (ADR 0043, CONFIG_MANAGE).

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.ReferenceScopeDirectoryIT
comment:
Proves the reference module's {@link com.kibootia.backend.reference.persistence.JpaScopeDirectory} meets the rules every {@link ScopeDirectory} must keep, against a real MySQL (integration contract, Timetia ADR 0004). The hooks create places with a chosen id directly in the tables, because production ids are generated; the provider's read path (tenant filtering, soft delete, exact code match) is the real one under test.

Each test runs under its own tenant, so nothing a test writes is visible to another, and a foreign-tenant place is written under a second tenant that the reads never bind. The tables are cleared when a fresh directory is asked for.

methods.name: insert
methods.comment: Writes a live place with the chosen id. A division and a batch carry a parent id; with no database foreign key in this slice, a placeholder parent is enough for a read test.

name: com.kibootia.backend.reference.TeachingAssignmentApiIT
comment: Drives the teaching-assignment API through the real stack (ADR 0043, CONFIG_MANAGE), proving the batch rule (theory names no batch; a lab names a batch of its division), reference validation and the duplicate guard.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.LiveTimetableApiIT
comment:
The live timetable through the real stack: what each role sees, and that a list and a single lecture agree. The campus is built through the APIs (see {@link TimetableApiTest}), people are given their roles as the screen does, and every answer comes from the real reference data, the real scope directory and the real decision point, so this is the proof that the authorization model works over HTTP and not only in unit tests.

The published timetable has 24 lectures: CSE-A has 20 (12 theory, 4 lab for batch A1, 4 lab for batch A2) and ME-A has 4 (theory). A theory lecture is for every batch of its division; a lab is for its one batch.

methods.name: listed
methods.comment: The IDs of the lectures the caller sees for the whole term.

methods.name: lectureOn
methods.comment: The ID of the first lecture of the division on the date, as the administrator sees it.

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.TimetableApiTest
comment:
The base of the timetable tests: a small campus built through the real APIs, with the real scope directory (not a fake), so what a test proves holds for the application as it runs. The campus:
  • department CSE holds division CSE-A, which has batches CSE-A1 and CSE-A2;
  • department ME holds division ME-A, which has batch ME-A1;
  • teachers Rao and Roy (CSE) and Mehta (ME), each with a user account, and four rooms;
  • the term SEM3, Monday 2026-07-06 to Friday 2026-07-31, so each weekday falls four times.

Teaching assignments: for CSE-A, OOP theory by Rao, DBMS theory by Roy, OOP lab for batch A1 by Rao and OOP lab for batch A2 by Roy (the two labs run in parallel); for ME-A, Thermodynamics theory by Mehta.

methods.name: buildCampus
methods.comment: One @BeforeEach, so that cleaning always runs before building (JUnit does not order several).

methods.name: draft
methods.comment: Creates a draft for the division in the term, taking effect on the date, and returns its ID.

methods.name: entry
methods.signature: entry(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, int, int, int, java.lang.String)
methods.comment: Adds an in-person lecture to a draft and returns the entry's ID.

methods.name: publishStandardTimetable
methods.comment: Publishes the standard timetable of both divisions, effective from the start of the term. CSE-A: Monday 9-10 OOP theory (R101), Monday 10-11 DBMS theory (R101), Tuesday 9-11 the two labs in parallel (LAB1 and R102), Wednesday 14-15 DBMS online. ME-A: Monday 9-10 Thermodynamics (R201). Each weekday falls four times in the term, so CSE-A has 20 lectures and ME-A has 4.

methods.name: create
methods.comment: POSTs as the administrator, expects 201 and returns the new resource's ID.

methods.name: somebody
methods.comment: A signed-in person with no role beyond the default one.

methods.name: personWith
methods.comment: A person given the role in a place by the administrator, as the screen does (no place for a global role).

name: com.kibootia.backend.timetable.TimetableAuthoringApiIT
comment: Arranging the base timetable through the real stack: versions, the weekly lectures of a draft, publishing and what it does to the dated lectures. The rules under test are the data model's: a published version is never edited, a version cannot book a teacher, a room or students twice, and a version that takes effect later replaces the earlier one from its date.
